page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.large is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, the instance provides dedicated CPU core execution with simultaneous multithreading. Memory provision stands at 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features no hardware graphics acceleration.

Benchmark measurements indicate entry-level compute capability. Across synthetic CPU workloads, the system recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 1089.08 and a multi-core score of 4315.32, placing it within the bottom quartile of evaluated systems. Geekbench testing returned scores of 873.0 in single-core and 2768.0 in multi-core metrics. In compression and decompression tests, single-threaded gzip throughput achieved 19.03 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 reached 7.2 GB/sec, positioning the instance in the lower tenth percentile for raw compute efficiency.

Memory and operational subsystems exhibit moderate throughput. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 32.61 GB/sec, while write bandwidth achieved 28.16 GB/sec, representing average performance within mid-tier bandwidth profiles. Redis SET operations registered at 5.02 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measured 3.54 GB/sec. Because local disk storage is absent, external network-attached volumes are necessary for persistent state operations.

Given its hardware specifications and measured performance indicators, Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.large is aligned with lightweight general-purpose computing requirements. Suitable applications include standard web serving, small staging environments, internal enterprise utility services, and modest background task processing where baseline Intel Xeon instruction sets such as AVX-512 are beneficial without requiring peak single-thread execution rates.
